criteria.false: no: moving or belting items that already exist from one place to another, fixing or refuelling, power, putting drills on ore, research, a question

chain.instructions: Does `order` ask for two or more different products, or for a production chain where one new machine's output feeds another new machine (an ingredient that isn't on the belts has to be made first)?

criteria.true: yes: 'make gears and pipes', red science (gears made first, then packs), green circuits from plates (cables made first), 'a science line with gears from the iron belt'
criteria.false: no: one product straight from what's on the belts: gears from iron plates, steel from iron plates, plates from ore, inserters from belts carrying plates, gears and circuits

elsewhere.instructions: Does `order` ask for the product to be taken on to some other place it names: a chest further away, a bus, another machine, a player?

criteria.true: yes: 'send the plates on a belt to the chest at [gps]', 'and send it to the mall'
criteria.false: no: it stays by the machines; 'into a chest', 'into a chest around [gps]', 'onto a belt' and naming which belt to build off don't count

criteria.false: no: moving or belting items that already exist from one place to another, fixing or refuelling, power, putting drills on ore, research, a question

chain.instructions: Does `order` ask for two or more different products, or for a production chain where one new machine's output feeds another new machine (an ingredient that isn't on the belts has to be made first)?

criteria.true: yes: 'make gears and pipes', red science (gears made first, then packs), green circuits from plates (cables made first), 'a science line with gears from the iron belt'
criteria.false: no: one product straight from what's on the belts: gears from iron plates, steel from iron plates, plates from ore, inserters from belts carrying plates, gears and circuits

elsewhere.instructions: Does `order` ask for the product to be taken on to some other place it names: a chest further away, a bus, another machine, a player?

criteria.true: yes: 'send the plates on a belt to the chest at [gps]', 'and send it to the mall'
criteria.false: no: it stays by the machines; 'into a chest', 'into a chest around [gps]', 'onto a belt' and naming which belt to build off don't count

state.order: @serf Two belts start here: iron plates at [gps=10,4] and copper plates at [gps=10,10], both running east, and there's a power pole at [gps=12,20]. Automate red science off them: at least 3 assemblers, packs onto a belt or into a chest.

build.instructions: Does `order` ask for something to be made (produced automatically) from what a belt carries, even if it doesn't say 'build' or name the machines?

chain.instructions: Does `order` ask for the product to feed further new machines that make something else from it, or for two different products?

criteria.false: no: the product just goes into chests or onto a belt; fuel taken from the belt; steel from iron plates and coal; inserters from belts of plates, gears and circuits

elsewhere.instructions: Does `order` ask for the product to be taken on to some other place it names: a chest further away, a bus, another machine, a player?

criteria.false: no: moving or belting items that already exist from one place to another, fixing or refuelling, power, putting drills on ore, research, a question

chain.instructions: Does `order` ask for the product to feed further new machines that make something else from it, or for two different products?

criteria.true: yes: 'gear production feeding a row of red science assemblers', 'a science line with gears from the iron belt', 'make gears and pipes'
criteria.false: no: the product just goes into chests or onto a belt; fuel taken from the belt; steel from iron plates and coal; inserters from belts of plates, gears and circuits

elsewhere.instructions: Does `order` ask for the product to be transported somewhere after it's made: run, belted, sent, carried or brought to some place?

criteria.true: yes: 'run them to the circuit build at [gps]', 'send the plates on a belt to the chest at [gps]', 'belt them over to the science', 'and bring them to me'
criteria.false: no: 'into a chest', 'into a chest around [gps]', 'gears into a chest by the machines', 'onto a belt', 'plates into chests'

onto_belt.instructions: Does `order` ask for the finished product to be put onto an output belt rather than into chests?

criteria.false: no: moving or belting items that already exist from one place to another, fixing or refuelling, power, putting drills on ore, research, a question

chain.instructions: Does `order` ask for the product to feed further new machines that make something else from it, or for two different products?

criteria.true: yes: 'gear production feeding a row of red science assemblers', 'a science line with gears from the iron belt', 'make gears and pipes'
criteria.false: no: the product just goes into chests or onto a belt; fuel taken from the belt; steel from iron plates and coal; inserters from belts of plates, gears and circuits

elsewhere.instructions: Does `order` ask for the product to be transported somewhere after it's made: run, belted, sent, carried or brought to some place?

criteria.true: yes: 'run them to the circuit build at [gps]', 'send the plates on a belt to the chest at [gps]', 'belt them over to the science', 'and bring them to me'
criteria.false: no: 'into a chest', 'into a chest around [gps]', 'gears into a chest by the machines', 'onto a belt', 'put it on a belt', 'plates into chests'

onto_belt.instructions: Does `order` ask for the finished product to be put onto an output belt rather than into chests?

criteria.true: yes: 'put the cable on a belt', 'gears onto a belt', 'output onto a belt'
criteria.false: no: building the machines on, off or along a belt; 'into a chest'; nothing said

criteria.false: no: moving or belting items that already exist from one place to another, fixing or refuelling, power, putting drills on ore, research, a question

chain.instructions: Does `order` ask for the product to feed further new machines that make something else from it, or for two different products?

criteria.true: yes: 'gear production feeding a row of red science assemblers', 'a science line with gears from the iron belt', 'make gears and pipes'
criteria.false: no: the product just goes into chests or onto a belt; fuel taken from the belt; steel from iron plates and coal; inserters from belts of plates, gears and circuits

elsewhere.instructions: Does `order` ask for the product to be transported somewhere after it's made: run, belted, sent, carried or brought to some place?

criteria.true: yes: 'run them to the circuit build at [gps]', 'send the plates on a belt to the chest at [gps]', 'belt them over to the science', 'and bring them to me'
criteria.false: no: 'into a chest', 'into a chest around [gps]', 'gears into a chest by the machines', 'onto a belt', 'put it on a belt', 'plates into chests'

onto_belt.instructions: Does `order` ask for the finished product to be put onto an output belt rather than into chests?

criteria.true: yes: 'put the cable on a belt', 'gears onto a belt', 'output onto a belt'
criteria.false: no: building the machines on, off or along a belt; 'into a chest'; nothing said

criteria.false: no: moving or belting items that already exist from one place to another, fixing or refuelling, power, putting drills on ore, research, a question

several.instructions: Does `order` ask for two or more different products?

criteria.true: yes: 'make gears and pipes', 'iron chests and pipes off the belt'
criteria.false: no: one product, even if something has to be made for it first (red science, green circuits)

onward.instructions: Does `order` ask for the product to feed further new machines that make something else from it?

criteria.true: yes: 'gear production feeding a row of red science assemblers', 'a science line with gears from the iron belt into the science assemblers'
criteria.false: no: the product goes into chests or onto a belt; 'automate red science off these belts'

elsewhere.instructions: Does `order` ask for the product to be transported somewhere after it's made: run, belted, sent, carried or brought to some place?

criteria.true: yes: 'run them to the circuit build at [gps]', 'send the plates on a belt to the chest at [gps]', 'belt them over to the science', 'and bring them to me'
criteria.false: no: 'into a chest', 'into a chest around [gps]', 'gears into a chest by the machines', 'onto a belt', 'put it on a belt', 'plates into chests'

onto_belt.instructions: Does `order` ask for the finished product to be put onto an output belt rather than into chests?

criteria.true: yes: 'put the cable on a belt', 'gears onto a belt', 'output onto a belt'
criteria.false: no: building the machines on, off or along a belt; 'into a chest'; nothing said

count.instructions: How many machines making the product itself does `order` ask for (not counting machines that make its ingredients)? Pick the number written in it ('at least 3' -> 3, 'one assembler' -> 1, '3 cable assemblers to 2 circuit assemblers' -> 2), or not_said.

criteria.not_said: the order doesn't say how many machines

state.order: @serf Iron plates come along the belt at [gps=10,4] and copper plates along [gps=10,10], both running east; power pole at [gps=12,20]. Automate green circuits off them. 3 cable assemblers to 2 circuit assemblers is the usual ratio.

build.instructions: Does `order` ask for something to be made (produced automatically) from what a belt carries, even if it doesn't say 'build' or name the machines?

criteria.true: yes: 'make gears off this belt', 'build 6 furnaces off the ore belt', 'set up an assembler making inserters', 'pipes off the iron belt please', 'copper cable please, off the copper belt'
criteria.false: no: moving or belting items that already exist from one place to another, fixing or refuelling, power, putting drills on ore, research, a question

several.instructions: Does `order` ask for two or more different products?

criteria.true: yes: 'make gears and pipes', 'iron chests and pipes off the belt'
criteria.false: no: one product, even if something has to be made for it first (red science, green circuits)

onward.instructions: Does `order` ask for the product to feed further new machines that make something else from it?

criteria.false: no: the product goes into chests or onto a belt; 'automate red science off these belts'

elsewhere.instructions: Does `order` ask for the product to be transported somewhere after it's made: run, belted, sent, carried or brought to some place?

criteria.true: yes: 'run them to the circuit build at [gps]', 'send the plates on a belt to the chest at [gps]', 'belt them over to the science', 'and bring them to me'

onto_belt.instructions: Does `order` ask for the finished product to be put onto an output belt rather than into chests?

criteria.false: no: building the machines on, off or along a belt; 'into a chest'; nothing said

product.instructions: Which of these does `order` ask to have made?

criteria.none_of_these: something not in this list, or two or more different products

count.instructions: How many machines making the product itself does `order` ask for (not counting machines that make its ingredients)? Pick the number written in it ('at least 3' -> 3, 'one assembler' -> 1, '3 cable assemblers to 2 circuit assemblers' -> 2), or not_said.

build.instructions: Does `order` ask for something to be made (produced automatically) from what a belt carries, even if it doesn't say 'build' or name the machines?

criteria.false: no: moving or belting items that already exist from one place to another, fixing or refuelling, power, putting drills on ore, research, a question

several.instructions: Does `order` ask for two or more DIFFERENT kinds of item to be made?

criteria.true: yes: 'make gears and pipes', 'iron chests and pipes off the belt'
criteria.false: no: one kind of item, whatever the plurals or how many machines and chests ('pipes, 3 assemblers, into chests'); one item even if something has to be made for it first (red science, green circuits)

onward.instructions: Does `order` ask for the product to feed further new machines that make something else from it?

criteria.true: yes: 'gear production feeding a row of red science assemblers', 'a science line with gears from the iron belt into the science assemblers'
criteria.false: no: the product goes into chests or onto a belt; 'automate red science off these belts'

count.instructions: How many machines making the product itself does `order` ask for (not counting machines that make its ingredients)? Pick the number written in it ('at least 3' -> 3, 'one assembler' -> 1, '3 cable assemblers to 2 circuit assemblers' -> 2), or not_said.

criteria.not_said: the order doesn't say how many machines

state.order: @serf copper cable please, off the copper belt at [gps=2,2], put it on a belt

build.instructions: Does `order` ask for something to be made (produced automatically) from what a belt carries, even if it doesn't say 'build' or name the machines?

criteria.true: yes: 'make gears off this belt', 'build 6 furnaces off the ore belt', 'set up an assembler making inserters', 'pipes off the iron belt please', 'copper cable please, off the copper belt'
criteria.false: no: moving or belting items that already exist from one place to another, fixing or refuelling, power, putting drills on ore, research, a question

several.instructions: Does `order` ask for two or more DIFFERENT kinds of item to be made?

criteria.true: yes: 'make gears and pipes', 'iron chests and pipes off the belt'
criteria.false: no: one kind of item, whatever the plurals or how many machines and chests ('pipes, 3 assemblers, into chests'); one item even if something has to be made for it first (red science, green circuits)

onward.instructions: Does `order` ask for the product to feed further new machines that make something else from it?

criteria.true: yes: 'gear production feeding a row of red science assemblers', 'a science line with gears from the iron belt into the science assemblers'
criteria.false: no: the product goes into chests or onto a belt; 'automate red science off these belts'

elsewhere.instructions: Does `order` ask for the product to be transported somewhere after it's made: run, belted, sent, carried or brought to some place?

criteria.true: yes: 'run them to the circuit build at [gps]', 'send the plates on a belt to the chest at [gps]', 'belt them over to the science', 'and bring them to me'
criteria.false: no: 'into a chest', 'into a chest around [gps]', 'gears into a chest by the machines', 'onto a belt', 'put it on a belt', 'plates into chests'

onto_belt.instructions: Does `order` ask for the finished product to be put onto an output belt rather than into chests?

criteria.true: yes: 'put the cable on a belt', 'gears onto a belt', 'output onto a belt'
criteria.false: no: building the machines on, off or along a belt; 'into a chest'; nothing said

criteria.false: no: building the machines on, off or along a belt; 'into a chest'; nothing said

product.instructions: Which of these does `order` ask to have made?

criteria.none_of_these: something not in this list, or two or more different products

count.instructions: How many machines making the product itself does `order` ask for (not counting machines that make its ingredients)? Pick the number written in it ('at least 3' -> 3, 'one assembler' -> 1, '3 cable assemblers to 2 circuit assemblers' -> 2), or not_said.

criteria.not_said: the order doesn't say how many machines

state.order: @serf Two belts start here: iron plates at [gps=10,4] and copper plates at [gps=10,10], both running east, and there's a power pole at [gps=12,20]. Automate red science off them: at least 3 assemblers, packs onto a belt or into a chest.

build.instructions: Does `order` ask for something to be made (produced automatically) from what a belt carries, even if it doesn't say 'build' or name the machines?

criteria.true: yes: 'make gears off this belt', 'build 6 furnaces off the ore belt', 'set up an assembler making inserters', 'pipes off the iron belt please', 'copper cable please, off the copper belt'
criteria.false: no: moving or belting items that already exist from one place to another, fixing or refuelling, power, putting drills on ore, research, a question

several.instructions: Does `order` ask for two or more DIFFERENT kinds of item to be made?

criteria.true: yes: 'make gears and pipes', 'iron chests and pipes off the belt'
criteria.false: no: one kind of item, whatever the plurals or how many machines and chests ('pipes, 3 assemblers, into chests'); one item even if something has to be made for it first (red science, green circuits)

onward.instructions: Does `order` ask for the product to feed further new machines that make something else from it?

criteria.true: yes: 'gear production feeding a row of red science assemblers', 'a science line with gears from the iron belt into the science assemblers'
criteria.false: no: the product goes into chests or onto a belt; 'automate red science off these belts'

elsewhere.instructions: Does `order` ask for the product to be transported somewhere after it's made: run, belted, sent, carried or brought to some place?

criteria.true: yes: 'run them to the circuit build at [gps]', 'send the plates on a belt to the chest at [gps]', 'belt them over to the science', 'and bring them to me'
criteria.false: no: 'into a chest', 'into a chest around [gps]', 'gears into a chest by the machines', 'onto a belt', 'put it on a belt', 'plates into chests'

criteria.false: no: one kind of item, whatever the plurals or how many machines and chests ('pipes, 3 assemblers, into chests'); one item even if something has to be made for it first (red science, green circuits)

onward.instructions: Does `order` ask for the product to feed further new machines that make something else from it?

criteria.true: yes: 'gear production feeding a row of red science assemblers', 'a science line with gears from the iron belt into the science assemblers'
criteria.false: no: the product goes into chests or onto a belt; 'automate red science off these belts'

elsewhere.instructions: Does `order` ask for the product to be transported somewhere after it's made: run, belted, sent, carried or brought to some place?

criteria.true: yes: 'run them to the circuit build at [gps]', 'send the plates on a belt to the chest at [gps]', 'belt them over to the science', 'and bring them to me'
criteria.false: no: 'into a chest', 'into a chest around [gps]', 'gears into a chest by the machines', 'onto a belt', 'put it on a belt', 'plates into chests'

onto_belt.instructions: Does `order` ask for the finished product to be put onto an output belt rather than into chests?

criteria.true: yes: 'put the cable on a belt', 'gears onto a belt', 'output onto a belt'
criteria.false: no: building the machines on, off or along a belt; 'into a chest'; nothing said

product.instructions: Which of these does `order` ask to have made?

criteria.false: no: moving or belting items that already exist from one place to another, fixing or refuelling, power, putting drills on ore, research, a question

several.instructions: Does `order` ask for two or more DIFFERENT kinds of item to be made?

criteria.true: yes: 'make gears and pipes', 'iron chests and pipes off the belt'
criteria.false: no: one kind of item, whatever the plurals or how many machines and chests ('pipes, 3 assemblers, into chests'); one item even if something has to be made for it first (red science, green circuits)

onward.instructions: Does `order` ask for the product to feed further new machines that make something else from it?

criteria.true: yes: 'gear production feeding a row of red science assemblers', 'a science line with gears from the iron belt into the science assemblers'
criteria.false: no: the product goes into chests or onto a belt; 'automate red science off these belts'

elsewhere.instructions: Does `order` ask for the product to be transported somewhere after it's made: run, belted, sent, carried or brought to some place?

criteria.true: yes: 'run them to the circuit build at [gps]', 'send the plates on a belt to the chest at [gps]', 'belt them over to the science', 'and bring them to me'
criteria.false: no: 'into a chest', 'into a chest around [gps]', 'gears into a chest by the machines', 'onto a belt', 'put it on a belt', 'plates into chests'

onto_belt.instructions: Does `order` ask for the finished product to be put onto an output belt rather than into chests?

criteria.true: yes: 'put the cable on a belt', 'gears onto a belt', 'output onto a belt'
criteria.false: no: building the machines on, off or along a belt; 'into a chest'; nothing said

product.instructions: Which of these does `order` ask to have made?

criteria.none_of_these: something not in this list, or two or more different products

count.instructions: How many machines making the product itself does `order` ask for (not counting machines that make its ingredients)? Pick the number written in it ('at least 3' -> 3, 'one assembler' -> 1, '3 cable assemblers to 2 circuit assemblers' -> 2), or not_said.

criteria.not_said: the order doesn't say how many machines

criteria.none_of_these: something not in this list, or two or more different products

count.instructions: How many machines making the product itself does `order` ask for (not counting machines that make its ingredients)? Pick the number written in it ('at least 3' -> 3, 'one assembler' -> 1, '3 cable assemblers to 2 circuit assemblers' -> 2), or not_said.

criteria.not_said: the order doesn't say how many machines

state.order: @serf what can you make from this belt [gps=1,1]?

build.instructions: Does `order` ask for something to be made (produced automatically) from what a belt carries, even if it doesn't say 'build' or name the machines?

criteria.true: yes: 'make gears off this belt', 'build 6 furnaces off the ore belt', 'set up an assembler making inserters', 'pipes off the iron belt please', 'copper cable please, off the copper belt'
criteria.false: no: moving or belting items that already exist from one place to another, fixing or refuelling, power, putting drills on ore, research, a question

several.instructions: Does `order` ask for two or more DIFFERENT kinds of item to be made?

criteria.true: yes: 'make gears and pipes', 'iron chests and pipes off the belt'
criteria.false: no: one kind of item, whatever the plurals or how many machines and chests ('pipes, 3 assemblers, into chests'); one item even if something has to be made for it first (red science, green circuits)

onward.instructions: Does `order` ask for the product to feed further new machines that make something else from it?

criteria.true: yes: 'gear production feeding a row of red science assemblers', 'a science line with gears from the iron belt into the science assemblers'
criteria.false: no: the product goes into chests or onto a belt; 'automate red science off these belts'

elsewhere.instructions: Does `order` ask for the product to be transported somewhere after it's made: run, belted, sent, carried or brought to some place?

criteria.true: yes: 'run them to the circuit build at [gps]', 'send the plates on a belt to the chest at [gps]', 'belt them over to the science', 'and bring them to me'
criteria.false: no: 'into a chest', 'into a chest around [gps]', 'gears into a chest by the machines', 'onto a belt', 'put it on a belt', 'plates into chests'

onto_belt.instructions: Does `order` ask for the finished product to be put onto an output belt rather than into chests?

criteria.true: yes: 'put the cable on a belt', 'gears onto a belt', 'output onto a belt'
criteria.false: no: building the machines on, off or along a belt; 'into a chest'; nothing said

criteria.false: no: one kind of item, whatever the plurals or how many machines and chests ('pipes, 3 assemblers, into chests'); one item even if something has to be made for it first (red science, green circuits)

onward.instructions: Does `order` ask for the product to feed further new machines that make something else from it?

criteria.true: yes: 'gear production feeding a row of red science assemblers', 'a science line with gears from the iron belt into the science assemblers'
criteria.false: no: the product goes into chests or onto a belt; 'automate red science off these belts'

elsewhere.instructions: Does `order` ask for the product to be transported somewhere after it's made: run, belted, sent, carried or brought to some place?

criteria.true: yes: 'run them to the circuit build at [gps]', 'send the plates on a belt to the chest at [gps]', 'belt them over to the science', 'and bring them to me'
criteria.false: no: 'into a chest', 'into a chest around [gps]', 'gears into a chest by the machines', 'onto a belt', 'put it on a belt', 'plates into chests'

onto_belt.instructions: Does `order` ask for the finished product to be put onto an output belt rather than into chests?

criteria.true: yes: 'put the cable on a belt', 'gears onto a belt', 'output onto a belt'
criteria.false: no: building the machines on, off or along a belt; 'into a chest'; nothing said

criteria.false: no: moving or belting items that already exist from one place to another, fixing or refuelling, power, putting drills on ore, research, a question

several.instructions: Does `order` ask for two or more DIFFERENT kinds of item to be made?

criteria.true: yes: 'make gears and pipes', 'iron chests and pipes off the belt'
criteria.false: no: one kind of item, whatever the plurals or how many machines and chests ('pipes, 3 assemblers, into chests'); one item even if something has to be made for it first (red science, green circuits)

onward.instructions: Does `order` ask for the product to feed further new machines that make something else from it?

criteria.true: yes: 'gear production feeding a row of red science assemblers', 'a science line with gears from the iron belt into the science assemblers'
criteria.false: no: the product goes into chests or onto a belt; 'automate red science off these belts'

elsewhere.instructions: Does `order` ask for the product to be transported somewhere after it's made: run, belted, sent, carried or brought to some place?

criteria.true: yes: 'run them to the circuit build at [gps]', 'send the plates on a belt to the chest at [gps]', 'belt them over to the science', 'and bring them to me'
criteria.false: no: 'into a chest', 'into a chest around [gps]', 'gears into a chest by the machines', 'onto a belt', 'put it on a belt', 'plates into chests'

onto_belt.instructions: Does `order` ask for the finished product to be put onto an output belt rather than into chests?

criteria.true: yes: 'put the cable on a belt', 'gears onto a belt', 'output onto a belt'
criteria.false: no: building the machines on, off or along a belt; 'into a chest'; nothing said

product.instructions: Which of these does `order` ask to have made?

criteria.steel-plate: steel plate (steel: furnaces on iron plates)
criteria.none_of_these: something not in this list, or two or more different products

count.instructions: How many machines making the product itself does `order` ask for (not counting machines that make its ingredients)? Pick the number written in it ('at least 3' -> 3, 'one assembler' -> 1, '3 cable assemblers to 2 circuit assemblers' -> 2), or not_said.

criteria.not_said: the order doesn't say how many machines

count.instructions: How many machines making the product itself does `order` ask for (not counting machines that make its ingredients)? Pick the number written in it ('at least 3' -> 3, 'one assembler' -> 1, '3 cable assemblers to 2 circuit assemblers' -> 2), or not_said.

criteria.not_said: the order doesn't say how many machines

state.order: @serf The belt at [gps=10,4] carries iron plates and gears (one lane each), and the one at [gps=10,10] carries circuits; both run east. Power pole at [gps=12,20]. Set up an assembler making inserters into a chest, fed from these belts.

build.instructions: Does `order` ask for something to be made (produced automatically) from what a belt carries, even if it doesn't say 'build' or name the machines?

criteria.true: yes: 'make gears off this belt', 'build 6 furnaces off the ore belt', 'set up an assembler making inserters', 'pipes off the iron belt please', 'copper cable please, off the copper belt'
criteria.false: no: moving or belting items that already exist from one place to another, fixing or refuelling, power, putting drills on ore, research, a question

several.instructions: Does `order` ask for two or more DIFFERENT kinds of item to be made?

criteria.true: yes: 'make gears and pipes', 'iron chests and pipes off the belt'
criteria.false: no: one kind of item, whatever the plurals or how many machines and chests ('pipes, 3 assemblers, into chests'); one item even if something has to be made for it first (red science, green circuits)

onward.instructions: Does `order` ask for the product to feed further new machines that make something else from it?

criteria.true: yes: 'gear production feeding a row of red science assemblers', 'a science line with gears from the iron belt into the science assemblers'
criteria.false: no: the product goes into chests or onto a belt; 'automate red science off these belts'

elsewhere.instructions: Does `order` ask for the product to be transported somewhere after it's made: run, belted, sent, carried or brought to some place?

criteria.true: yes: 'run them to the circuit build at [gps]', 'send the plates on a belt to the chest at [gps]', 'belt them over to the science', 'and bring them to me'
criteria.false: no: 'into a chest', 'into a chest around [gps]', 'gears into a chest by the machines', 'onto a belt', 'put it on a belt', 'plates into chests'

onto_belt.instructions: Does `order` ask for the finished product to be put onto an output belt rather than into chests?

criteria.true: yes: 'put the cable on a belt', 'gears onto a belt', 'output onto a belt'
criteria.false: no: building the machines on, off or along a belt; 'into a chest'; nothing said
